content:
The Bahrain Grand Prix will be broadcast live for free on Apple TV this weekend, with no subscription required.

Normally, watching F1 on Apple TV requires a paid subscription, but this weekend anyone can tune in for free. You can start by watching the replay of qualifying to get ready for the main race, which goes live in the early hours of this morning, with the race scheduled to start at 3 a.m. Eastern Time.

To watch the race, you only need to download the Apple TV app on a compatible device, be in the United States, and stay up late for the live broadcast.

The broadcast coverage begins at 1:50 a.m. Eastern Time, with the main race set to start at 3 a.m. Eastern Time. Of course, if you want to get to bed earlier, you can also catch up later via on-demand streaming.

You can download the Apple TV app on Apple devices, Amazon Fire Stick, Roku, PlayStation, Xbox, Android, and more, or watch it via web browser at tv.apple.com.

With qualifying having taken place earlier, Red Bull's Max Verstappen secured pole position for the first time this season, Lewis Hamilton took second, and championship leader Kim Antonelli lined up third. This is Red Bull's best chance of taking a race win so far this year.

You may be wondering why the Bahrain Grand Prix is being held in Malaysia. In a normal season, the Bahrain round would take place at the start of the season, but due to the ongoing conflict in Iran, the event was forced to be cancelled, and Bahrain's organisers decided instead to sponsor a race held elsewhere in the world.

Although Sepang is no longer on the official F1 calendar, the circuit remains hugely popular with fans, and an exciting, close-fought race is expected.

Just a reminder: you can watch the race for free on the Apple TV app without a subscription. The main race starts at 3 a.m. Eastern Time, with broadcast coverage beginning at 1:50 a.m. Eastern Time.
